newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for May 6.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for May 6.

text.p: Mexican crude port Dos Bocas remained shut on Tuesday to crude exports, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1500 GMT daily meteorological report.

The Gulf of Mexico port originally shut on Saturday afternoon, reopened at 1825 local/2325 GMT on Monday and closed again at 0615 local/1115 GMT Tuesday to crude exports. Tugboats that guide the tankers could not operate because of waves eight to ten feet high, a port official told Reuters.
The regional cold front has relaxed in intensity since the weekend, with strongest winds along the Yucatan peninsula.

Salina Cruz port in Oaxaca was closed to smaller ships, such as tourism and fishing craft, amid winds of up to 72 km per hour, the report said. Smaller ships were warned against sailing along the coasts of Oaxaca and Chiapas states and along the Yucatan peninsula.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.

Some clouds and possible rains, winds from 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 km/11 to 22 miles per hour) with waves three to six feet high. Rains and waves up to seven feet high along Oaxaca and Chiapas coasts. -- Gulf of Mexico:

Isolated light rains along the coast, winds in general from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour), except along Yucatan peninsula where winds from east at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves five to seven feet high.
Hot and clear to partly cloudy with isolated rains. Winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
